items.title: 68163_Tom Whaley oral history interview
items.q: Mrs. Anderson would say--that's the lady owned it--she would come out and say, 'oh, Mr. Whaley, would you please give us some music?'

ctx.x: Yeah. he used to come in there on Sunday afternoons, see, when he was in Boston. He'd come down there in the afternoons, and we'd drink champagne, and when he got through, he'd give us $200, to divide this among the group.

We used to make good money--if we didn't make $35 a night, nearly every night-- if people didn't give us any money, we'd go by the bar and hang out at the bar, and Mrs. Anderson would say--that's the lady owned it--she would come out and say, "oh, Mr. Whaley, would you please give us some music?" And I'd say, "Well, these people aint interested in--they're only interested in their own selves. They don't want our music." But I said, "Well, all right. We'll do it. We'll accommodate you." We'd go back there--shucks.…

We used to have this old man, he used to come down here. He was a sharp mother. He must have been five feet, and he'd have a frock coat on--big--and he would come in and, say, --and reach in his pocket and he'd have a billfold and he would whip it out and he'd be looking for a $10 bill. See, he'd give $10 bills, and say, "Play 'Dixie'." And we'd play "Dixie" a couple of times, see, and he'd come back and say "Play 'Dixie,' to give him some more, see, and all the people would do that much; they'd say, "Is that all…
